content:
When reviewing nightly-testing PRs into bump/v4.xx.yy branches GitHub tends to choke on the thousands of commits in the history. Git can't see that there are only a couple commits per PR that are actually relevant, since all the history gets squashed whenever the previous PR is merged via bors. We already merge the master branch (automatically) so enabling merges from bump/nightly-20x6-yy-zz shouldn't introduce any more complexity in the history.

I wonder if we also can avoid a few merge conflicts this way, since there would be a lot fewer commits since the last common ancestor? (At the very least, this should not make the situation any worse.)

The nightly infrastructure/workflow changes I'm working on right now should also solve this issue, so maybe it's not worth the effort to fix right now?

(I want to replace the nightly-testing branch by downstream-lean4, which will then open regular adaptation PRs for review to a bump/vX.Y.Z branch still living in mathlib.)
Hmm, could you explain a bit more about the changes that your plan makes?

On every release, a bump/v4.X.0 branch for the next release is created as usual. Then, whenever downstream-lean4 contains changes that are not yet in the bump branch and its CI for mathlib is green, it creates a PR to the bump branch. The PR would contain

  1. a commit merging master into the bump branch,
  2. a commit applying all the downstream-lean4 adaptations, and maybe
  3. a commit where lake update was run.

Of course, 2. must be a separate commit so there's a chance to actually review the adaptations.

With this approach, the bump branch CI should stay green in-between downstream PRs. The bump branch history should also stay fairly simple. I think it would make sense to merge/rebase the downstream PRs instead of squashing, so you don't lose the distinction between "changes from master" and "adaptation changes".

Ah I see, that makes sense! I wonder if this is going to be the best workflow though: my experience is commenting on a commit diff in GitHub is a lot more friction and less visible than commenting on a PR diff. I can't easily come up with a better solution without more branches though. (In the direction of: continue merging things automatically into bump/v4.X.0, but then have a bump/v4.X.0-green branch that gets fast-forwarded only when CI passes on the bump/v4.X.0 branch.) I suppose it depends what we want to use the bump branch for apart from merging into master at the end of the month.
I wanted to avoid the bump branch having red CI, but maybe it would make sense to just push the merge commit (1.) directly, and then only have 2. and 3. in the PR.
